jd:
Android engineer
Mid
Product-led SaaS company shipping internal Android tools. A small mobile team owns Kotlin + Jetpack Compose apps so feature teams can expose status and summary screens without pulling in Flutter or a WebView shell. Hiring to strengthen day-to-day Android app work on that team.

Day to day:
- Implement and review Compose screens in Gradle Android projects
- Parse operational CSV extracts and return stable summary values on screen
- Keep Home, Status, and Summary destinations predictable for QA and staging builds
- Pair with mobile engineers on assemble, Gradle, and “works on my machine” issues
- Improve shared Compose templates and Gradle conventions

Required skills:
- Comfortable building Android with Gradle (assembleDebug)
- Can implement Jetpack Compose screens that bind string resources and computed state
- Can parse a simple CSV and aggregate numeric columns with defined skip/tie rules
- Can validate a debug build (and optional unit tests) against the documented UI contract

Nice to have:
- Familiarity with Android Studio and the API 35 SDK / emulator
- Experience with Compose Material 3
- Prior work on internal platform or developer-experience Android apps
- Comfort reading Gradle compiler output when a build fails

Constraints:
- Assessment focuses on completing the provided Gradle + Jetpack Compose app — not redesigning the stack or adding Flutter, React Native, or a WebView
- Do not test Play Store publishing, CI pipelines, or cloud backends in this challenge
- Candidate works in a desktop environment with Terminal, Android Studio, OpenJDK 17, and the Android SDK available
- Starter files on the desktop are shared scenery; do not require inventing a different UI toolkit
prompt: A small Kotlin + Jetpack Compose app is on your desktop. The Gradle project already compiles and wires Home, Status, and Summary tabs. Your job is to implement the stubbed screens and Summary.fromCsv so those destinations show the documented greeting, status copy, and CSV summary.
